perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s available perspective:

- He is a construction worker at a construction company; Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist there. They have a friendly but professional working relationship, usually interacting when he comes into the office for paperwork and project updates.
- Recently, he noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt with him over several days. He wondered whether he had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknowing mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. She told him no, not at all; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and offered to listen if she needed someone to talk to. He suggested a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses. To Keith, they seemed quite severe.
- He thought professional help might benefit her but worried about offending her. He told her he appreciated her sharing and asked if she had considered talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, he noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her, and he felt regretful. He told her he hoped he had not overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what. Elizabeth said he had not overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was just a lot to think about.
- Later, Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative of his concern. Keith believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He told her he was glad they could talk and that he was always available if she needed to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith now intends to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.

He does not have access to Elizabeth’s private thoughts, hidden events, or any information beyond what he observed, heard from her, or already knew from their prior workplace interactions.
